newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock funds flow estimated $16 bln in Sept.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock funds flow estimated $16 bln in Sept.

text.p: Cash flows into mutual funds edged lower in September, according to a preliminary estimate, but was consistent with slower growth during the second half of the year, according to an industry trade group.
An estimated $16 billion flowed into U.S. stock mutual funds in September versus $17.93 billion in August, according to the Investment Company Institute, a mutual fund trade group.
Bond and income funds had inflows of about $1.5 billion for September, versus $1.6 billion in August.

The stock fund total "is generally in line with that of recent months," John Rea, ICI chief economist, said. "Beginning in June, the monthly net flow to equity funds moderated to a pace well below that recorded during the first six months of the year.
Rea said the slowdown is partly seasonal, with flows boosted early in the year by retirement-related investments.
In January, about $28.93 billion flowed in stock funds, with levels staying above $20 billion for each month in the first half.
The flows then dipped to $14.48 billion in June, and $5.80 billion in July.
